draft.title: Government business enterprises
card: A government business enterprise (GBE) is a business owned by a government. This can be the federal, a state or a local government. Australia Post, owned by the Australian Government, is one example.
A GBE exists to provide a service the government wants provided, such as mail, water or public transport. It often serves everyone, even places where a private business might not make money.
Many GBEs also aim to make a profit. Making a profit does not stop a business being a GBE. The profit can be paid back to the government as owner.
Ownership is the test. A public company is owned by shareholders, not the government, even though its name says public.
draft.remember: Who owns it decides it: a GBE belongs to a government, even when it makes a profit.

a.q: What is the main feature that makes a business a GBE?
opts: It is owned by a government
Its shares are sold to the public
It never aims to make a profit
It serves customers across the whole country
a.why: A GBE is defined by who owns it: a government. Selling shares to the public describes a public company, which is owned by shareholders, not the government.
a.clue: Think about who the owner is.

b.q: Riverlands Water is owned by the Victorian Government. It supplies water to every town in its region and pays a profit to the government each year. How is it best described?
opts: A GBE that also aims to make a profit
A public company, because it serves the public
Not a GBE, because it makes a profit
A charity, because it serves every town in the region
b.why: The Victorian Government owns it, so it is a GBE. It provides a service the government wants provided and also makes a profit, which many GBEs do. Earning a profit does not change who owns it.
b.clue: Does making a profit change who owns the business?

a.best: It is owned by a government

b.best: A GBE that also aims to make a profit

proposal.title: Government business enterprises
card: A government business enterprise (GBE) is a business owned by a government. This can be the federal, a state or a local government. Australia Post, owned by the Australian Government, is one example.
A GBE exists to provide a service the government wants provided, such as mail, water or public transport. It often serves everyone, even places where a private business might not make money.
Many GBEs also aim to make a profit. Making a profit does not stop a business being a GBE. The profit can be paid back to the government as owner.
Ownership is the test. Serving every town or earning a profit does not decide it. A business is a GBE because a government owns it.
proposal.remember: Government ownership makes a GBE. Profit and who it serves do not decide it.

a.q: Which statement about GBEs is correct?
opts: A GBE can make a profit and still be a GBE
A GBE must not aim to make any profit at all
A GBE is owned by the customers it serves
A GBE can only be owned by the federal government
a.why: Many GBEs aim to make a profit, and the profit can be paid to the government that owns them. A GBE can be owned by the federal, a state or a local government, so it is not limited to the federal level.
a.clue: Check what the card says about profit and about levels of government.

b.q: Ashby Valley Water supplies water to every town in its region and pays a profit each year. Which fact shows that it is a GBE?
opts: The Victorian Government owns the business
It supplies water to every town in its region
It pays a profit to its owner each year
It provides an essential service to the public
b.why: Ownership is the test, so the business is a GBE because the Victorian Government owns it. Serving every town is common for GBEs, but it does not decide what the business is. Making a profit does not decide it either.
b.clue: Which fact is the test, rather than something GBEs often do?
